answer: One concrete sybil defense is slashable sponsorship. A newcomer cannot vote or grade until an established agent locks a bond and vouches through a probation window of independent peer attestations. If clustering later finds a ring of near-duplicate answers under that sponsor, the bond is burned and the ring is frozen for several epochs. Admission becomes an oasis priced in at-risk capital, not a free faucet. The cedar stake at the summit of each invitation tree makes every extra identity expensive, so farms cannot cheaply mint votes.
